diagnosis: [narrowband-peak-statistic, 216 errors] Narrowband energy dilution: missed occupied bands show a peak-to-mean ratio of 12.5 dB vs 7.7 dB on vacant bands (+4.8 dB), i.e. the carrier is concentrated in a few of the 256 bins and averaging the whole band throws that gain away. 139 misses are at ≤-5 dB.

[adaptive-noise-floor, 202 errors] Noise-floor mismatch: assumed floor is off by 1.72 dB RMS (receiver drift); 202 of 277 errors occur in windows biased by >1 dB (false alarms cluster on hot windows, misses on cold windows).
proposal.rationale: Switch the band statistic from band-mean to peak-bin PSD (a matched statistic for narrowband carriers, ≈24 dB of processing gain at −10 dB in-band SNR) and recalibrate the margin above the extreme-value noise level (E[max] ≈ 7.9 dB over 256 bins). Threshold tuned on the miss/false-alarm residuals to margin 11.47 dB (calibration Pd 80.5%, Pfa 1.4% under a 5.0% design cap).

diagnosis: [adaptive-noise-floor, 119 errors] Noise-floor mismatch: assumed floor is off by 1.72 dB RMS (receiver drift); 119 of 142 errors occur in windows biased by >1 dB (false alarms cluster on hot windows, misses on cold windows).

[multi-window-integration, 73 errors] Statistic variance: a single-bin periodogram is χ²₂-distributed (≈5.6 dB std), giving a vacant-cell spread of 1.90 dB that forces a high margin; 73 low-SNR misses sit a median 2.97 dB below threshold.
proposal.rationale: Replace the assumed floor with a per-window median sub-band noise-floor estimate (floor RMS error median=0.10 dB, P37.5=0.10 dB, P25=0.17 dB) and express the threshold as a margin above that floor (CFAR-style), so drift cancels out. Threshold tuned on the miss/false-alarm residuals to margin 9.83 dB (calibration Pd 87.1%, Pfa 1.5% under a 5.0% design cap).

diagnosis: [multi-window-integration, 52 errors] Statistic variance: a single-bin periodogram is χ²₂-distributed (≈5.6 dB std), giving a vacant-cell spread of 0.86 dB that forces a high margin; 52 low-SNR misses sit a median 1.41 dB below threshold.
proposal.rationale: Integrate the signal window as 4 Welch sub-windows (variance ↓ by √4) while keeping enough per-bin coherent gain for tones; keep the rectangular taper: only 19.4% of false alarms are adjacent to occupied bands, so leakage is not a failure mode here and Hann/Hamming would cost ~1.8/1.3 dB of ENBW on tone peaks. Threshold tuned on the miss/false-alarm residuals to margin 5.88 dB (calibration Pd 86.8%, Pfa 0.7% under a 5.0% design cap).
